# core:prng

Seedable, reproducible pseudo-randomness for simulation, sampling,
procedural generation, randomized algorithms and tests.

Three layers that do not mix. [`Rng`] answers "the next value" one word at a
time and carries the derived uniform operations. [`VectorRng`] answers with
sixteen words at once, for a consumer that has use for all of them.
[`Squares64`] answers "the value at this key", so the draw order belongs to
the caller and nothing is carried between calls.

A [`Seed`] is data and every constructor of one is arithmetic, so nothing
here declares an effect. Entropy lives one module away: `core:secure_random`
exports `seed()`, which carries `Random`.

Nothing here is cryptographic. These generators are built to pass
statistical tests at the least work per word, not to resist an adversary who
has seen their output. A token, a session identifier, a nonce, a salt or a
key comes from `core:secure_random`.

An algorithm named in a type is fixed: [`Xoshiro256pp`] emits what
xoshiro256++ emits, for a given state, forever. Everything else — how a
`Seed` becomes a state, what [`split`](Seed::split) derives, how the derived
layer consumes draws — may change between releases.

## Synopsis

```wado
let mut rng = Xoshiro256pp::from_seed(Seed::from_u64(42));

let die = rng.random_range(1..=6);
assert 1 <= die <= 6;
assert 0.0 <= rng.random_f64() < 1.0;

let mut deck: List<i32> = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
rng.shuffle(&mut deck);
assert deck.len() == 5;

// The same seed replays the same stream, with no capability to declare.
let mut again = Xoshiro256pp::from_seed(Seed::from_u64(42));
assert again.random_range(1..=6) == die;
```

## Traits

### `pub trait Seedable with ()`

A generator that can be built from a [`Seed`].

#### `fn from_seed(seed: Seed) -> Self`

### `pub trait Rng with ()`

A scalar generator: one `u64` per draw, plus the uniform operations derived
from it. A shape other than uniform is a distribution and does not live here.

#### `fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64`

The next 64 bits of the stream, every bit of them usable.

#### `fn random_range<S: SampleRange>(&mut self, range: S) -> S::Value`

A uniform value from `low..<high` or `low..=high`, by Lemire's
multiply-shift with the rare rejection.

#### `fn random_f64(&mut self) -> f64`

A uniform `f64` in `[0, 1)`, from the draw's top 53 bits.

#### `fn random_bool(&mut self) -> bool`

`true` or `false` with equal probability, from one bit of the draw.

#### `fn shuffle<T>(&mut self, items: &mut List<T>)`

Permute `items` in place, uniformly over all permutations (Fisher-Yates).

#### `fn choose<T>(&mut self, items: &List<T>) -> Option<T>`

A uniformly chosen element of `items`, or `None` when it is empty.

### `pub trait SampleRange with ()`

A range that [`random_range`](Rng::random_range) can draw from: `..<` or
`..=` over any [`SampleUniform`] type.

#### `fn sample_from<R: Rng>(&self, rng: &mut R) -> Self::Value`

### `pub trait SampleUniform with ()`

An integer type a uniform range can be drawn over.

#### `fn sample_inclusive<R: Rng>(rng: &mut R, low: Self, high: Self) -> Self`

#### `fn sample_exclusive<R: Rng>(rng: &mut R, low: Self, high: Self) -> Self`

### `pub trait VectorRng with ()`

A lane-parallel generator: sixteen `u64` per call, as eight `u64x2`. The
width is the library's, not the engine's, so a consumer keeps no cursor.

#### `fn next_batch(&mut self) -> [u64x2, u64x2, u64x2, u64x2, u64x2, u64x2, u64x2, u64x2]`

## Structs

### `pub struct Seed`

Two hundred and fifty-six bits of well-distributed state, and the one input
every engine here takes. Nothing about it is secret.

_Fields are private._

#### `pub fn from_u64(n: u64) -> Seed`

Expand one number into a seed, through SplitMix64.
`Seed::from_u64(0)` is as good a seed as any other.

#### `pub fn from_bytes<B: AsByteSlice>(bytes: &B) -> Seed`

Absorb any byte source — a `ByteList`, a `ByteSlice`, or a `String`'s
UTF-8 bytes — into a seed.

#### `pub fn from_str(s: &String) -> Seed`

Absorb a string's bytes into a seed, so a world can be named rather than
numbered.

#### `pub fn split(&self, index: u64) -> Seed`

Derive an independent child seed at `index`. Worker _n_ derives its own
with no coordination; independence is statistical, not proven.

### `pub struct Xoshiro256pp`

xoshiro256++ (Blackman & Vigna): four words, shifts, xors and two rotates.
Period 2^256 - 1, and every 4-tuple of consecutive outputs appears once over it.

_Fields are private._

#### `pub fn jump(&mut self)`

Advance 2^128 steps, in the time 256 steps take. Two streams a jump
apart are disjoint for 2^128 draws apiece — proven, not hoped for.

#### `pub fn long_jump(&mut self)`

The same, 2^192 steps on.

#### `impl Seedable for Xoshiro256pp`

##### `fn from_seed(seed: Seed) -> Xoshiro256pp`

#### `impl Rng for Xoshiro256pp`

##### `fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64`

### `pub struct Squares64`

Squares (Widynski, arXiv:2004.06278): the value at a counter, not the next
one. A revisit regenerates it, and no two callers need agree on draw order.

_Fields are private._

#### `pub fn at(&self, counter: u64) -> u64`

The value at `counter`. Distinct counters give unrelated values; the
same counter always gives the same one.

#### `impl Seedable for Squares64`

##### `fn from_seed(seed: Seed) -> Squares64`

### `pub struct XoshiroSimd`

xoshiro256++ in eight lanes at once. Each lane starts 2^128 steps past the
one before, so the eight streams are disjoint for 2^128 draws apiece.

_Fields are private._

### `pub struct Shishua`

SHISHUA: the fastest generator here, and vector-only, since its round is
eight vectors wide and nothing smaller exists inside it. It has no jump.

_Fields are private._
